$ bend 
[exit 2]
bend — read and change a repository's issues, whatever tracker holds them.

The tracker is detected from the folder you are in. Commands, fields and
output are the same for every tracker. Where a tracker has no home for
something, bend keeps it in a fitting place or says so; it never drops it
silently. Run `bend status` to see what applies here.

Usage:
  bend <command> [arguments] [options]

Find and read:
  list [options]           List issues (open ones, not in Someday, unless --status says otherwise)
  ready [options]          List issues that can be worked on now
  show <id> [options]      Show one issue in full, with its links and sub-issues
  comments <id>            Show an issue's comments, oldest first
  search <text> [options]  Find issues by words in the title or id

Create and change:
  create <title> [options]  Create an issue
  edit <id> [options]       Change title, type, priority, category, assignee, labels or kept data
  write <id> <part> [text]  Replace one written part of an issue
  comment <id> [text]       Add a comment
  note <id> [text]          Add to an issue's notes, keeping what is there
  decide <id> [text]        Record a decision and its reason
  start <id>                Mark an issue as being worked on
  stop <id>                 Put an issue that is in progress back to open
  close <id> [options]      Close an issue
  reopen <id>               Reopen a closed issue
  defer <id>                Put an issue in Someday, set aside for later
  undefer <id>              Bring an issue back from Someday

Structure:
  move <id> (--under <parent> | --top)  Put an issue under a parent, or back at the top level
  link <id> <other-id> --kind <kind>    Link two issues
  unlink <id> <other-id> [options]      Remove the link between two issues

Finishing:
  handover <id> --done <text> --checked <text> --not-checked <text>  Hand an issue over to the owner to validate

About this repository:
  status [options]                                            Which tracker is used here and what it supports
  remember <text> [--key <key>]                               Save a standing fact for future sessions
  recall [words]                                              Show saved facts, all or those containing the words
  facts (--list | --ensure | --add-file <file> | --move-old)  Look after the facts file, for a program that sets a repository up
  refresh                                                     Reread the local copy of the issues from the tracker
  sync [options]                                              Sync the issues with their remote now, or say how the syncing stands
  helper [stop | start | disable | enable]                    The process that syncs the issues on a clock: how it stands, and stopping it
  refused [options]                                           List the changes a hosted tracker refused for good, and dismiss or resend them
  setup [step | all] [options]                                See what a repository needs to be ready, and set it up step by step
  version                                                     Which bend this is

Options for every command:
  -C, --dir <path>     Run as if started in <path>
      --json           Print machine-readable JSON
      --text-file <f>  Read the text argument from a file ("-" for stdin)
      --as <name>      Who is acting, for the tracker's history
  -h, --help           Help for bend or for one command

Exit status: 0 done · 1 refused, with the reason in plain words
             2 usage error · 3 not supported by this repository's tracker

Examples:
  bend ready
  bend show APP-142
  bend create "Login fails on Safari" --type bug --priority 1
  bend write APP-142 plan --text-file plan.md
  bend decide APP-142 "Keep the old endpoint, because mobile still calls it"
  bend link APP-150 APP-142 --kind blocked-by

Run `bend <command> --help` for one command.

bend — read and change a repository's issues, whatever tracker holds them.

$ bend list --help
[exit 0]
List issues (open ones, not in Someday, unless --status says otherwise).

Usage:
  bend list [options]

Options:
  --status <status>       open | in_progress | deferred | closed | … | all
  --type <type>           Only this type
  --priority <0-4>        Only this priority
  --category <name>       Only this category
  --assignee <name>       Only issues assigned to this person
  --parent <id>           Only the direct sub-issues of <id>
  --changed-since <time>  Only issues changed at or after this moment (ISO date and time)
  --with-body             With --json: add each issue's body (description and requirements as one text)
  --fresh                 Reread the local copy from the tracker first

Options for every command:

      --as <name>      Who is acting, for the tracker's history

$ bend write --help
[exit 0]
Replace one written part of an issue.

Usage:
  bend write <id> <part> [text]

Parts: description | requirements | done | plan | notes | body.
The text replaces what was there; an empty text clears the part.
For long text use --text-file.
The body is the description and the requirements as one text, the
requirements in a marked section; a program that shows the two together
writes them together.

Options for every command:
  -C, --dir <path>     Run as if started in <path>
      --json           Print machine-readable JSON
      --text-file <f>  Read the text argument from a file ("-" for stdin)
      --as <name>      Who is acting, for the tracker's history
  -h, --help           Help for bend or for one command

$ bend defer --help
[exit 0]
Put an issue in Someday, set aside for later.

Usage:
  bend defer <id>

A deferred issue is neither ready nor closed: `bend ready` and the default
`bend list` leave it out, and nothing starts it by itself. `bend undefer`
brings it back. On beads it is beads' own deferred status; on GitHub
issues, the label someday.

Options for every command:
  -C, --dir <path>     Run as if started in <path>
      --json           Print machine-readable JSON
      --text-file <f>  Read the text argument from a file ("-" for stdin)
      --as <name>      Who is acting, for the tracker's history
  -h, --help           Help for bend or for one command

$ bend link --help
[exit 0]
Link two issues.

Usage:
  bend link <id> <other-id> --kind <kind>

Kinds: blocked-by | discovered-from | related, and any kind of the
tracker's own that `bend status` lists.
Read it as a sentence: `bend link A B --kind blocked-by` records that A is blocked by B.

Options:
  --kind <kind>  blocked-by | discovered-from | related | one of the tracker's own

$ bend handover --help
[exit 0]
Hand an issue over to the owner to validate.

Usage:
  bend handover <id> --done <text> --checked <text> --not-checked <text>

All three are required. If everything was checked, say so: --not-checked "nothing".
The issue is left in progress; the owner validates and closes it.

Options:
  --done <text>         What was done
  --checked <text>      How it was checked
  --not-checked <text>  What was not checked

Options for every command:
  -C, --dir <path>     Run as if started in <path>
      --json           Print machine-readable JSON
      --text-file <f>  Read the text argument from a file ("-" for stdin)
      --as <name>      Who is acting, for the tracker's history
  -h, --help           Help for bend or for one command

$ bend facts --help
[exit 0]
Look after the facts file, for a program that sets a repository up.

Usage:
  bend facts (--list | --ensure | --add-file <file> | --move-old)

It works on the folder it is run in, which needs no tracker.
--list shows the facts in that folder's own file.
--ensure makes FACTS.md when there is none.
--add-file saves several facts at once, read as a JSON list of {"key": …, "text": …}.
--move-old moves facts still kept in the old section of AGENTS.md into FACTS.md.

Options:
  --list             Show the facts kept in this folder
  --ensure           Make the facts file when it is missing
  --add-file <file>  Save the facts in a JSON file ("-" for stdin)
  --move-old         Move facts out of the old section of AGENTS.md

Options for every command:
  -C, --dir <path>     Run as if started in <path>
      --json           Print machine-readable JSON
      --text-file <f>  Read the text argument from a file ("-" for stdin)
      --as <name>      Who is acting, for the tracker's history
  -h, --help           Help for bend or for one command

$ bend sync --help
[exit 0]
Sync the issues with their remote now, or say how the syncing stands.

Usage:
  bend sync [options]

Sends what was changed here and brings in what changed elsewhere, and says
how it ended (synced, failed, busy, conflict, stuck), what was sent and what
came in. Every sync, whoever started it, leaves an entry in a log kept with
the repository.

bend also syncs by itself: a helper process, which any bend command starts,
syncs every three minutes and ends when bend has not been used for half an
hour (`bend helper`). On a hosted tracker (GitHub issues) a change is also
sent a moment after the command that made it.

On a hosted tracker, changes that cannot be sent now (no network, a limit)
keep waiting and are sent by the next sync, in the order they were made;
`bend refused` lists the ones the tracker refused for good.

Exit status 1 when the sync did not work; the report is printed all the same.

Options:
  --status        Sync nothing: say what the issues are synced with, what waits, how the last sync ended, and what is wrong
  --log           Sync nothing: list the syncs made, newest first
  --failed        With --log: only the syncs that did not work
  --all           Reread every issue, which also drops the ones deleted on a hosted tracker (done by itself once a day)
  --no-wait       Do nothing if another sync is running, instead of waiting for it
  --cause <what>  What set it off, for the log: asked (the default) | timer | change | read

Options for every command:
  -C, --dir <path>     Run as if started in <path>
      --json           Print machine-readable JSON
      --text-file <f>  Read the text argument from a file ("-" for stdin)
      --as <name>      Who is acting, for the tracker's history
  -h, --help           Help for bend or for one command

$ bend refused --help
[exit 0]
List the changes a hosted tracker refused for good, and dismiss or resend them.

Usage:
  bend refused [options]

A change GitHub will never accept (the issue is gone or locked, the text is
too long) is taken out of the waiting changes and kept here, with GitHub's
reason and the text it carried, so that nothing written is lost. The issue
shows GitHub's version again.

Options:
  --dismiss <number|all>  Take a refused change off the list
  --again <number|all>    Put a refused change back among the waiting ones, to be sent once more

Options for every command:
  -C, --dir <path>     Run as if started in <path>
      --json           Print machine-readable JSON
      --text-file <f>  Read the text argument from a file ("-" for stdin)
      --as <name>      Who is acting, for the tracker's history
  -h, --help           Help for bend or for one command

$ bend setup --help
[exit 0]
See what a repository needs to be ready, and set it up step by step.

Usage:
  bend setup [step | all] [options]

Alone, it only reads: every step, whether it is done, and the command for
each one that is missing. With a step's name it does that step; `all` does
every missing one in order.

Steps: tracker | program | issues | instructions | facts | publish.
  tracker       choose beads or GitHub issues, recorded in .bend.json
  program       install the tracker's own program (beads)
  issues        beads: get the repository's issues, or start a database;
                GitHub: sign in
  instructions  write the rules for agents into AGENTS.md, and take out
                what beads wrote
  facts         carry facts saved in beads over to FACTS.md
  publish       publish the issue database to the repository's remote

A step asks what it needs to know, and shows what it will do before it
does it. Give the answers as options to run it without questions. Where
nobody is at the keyboard a step never waits: it changes nothing and says
which option was missing. A step that is already done changes nothing.

Airbender is for repositories of your own. Where origin is a fork, or a
GitHub repository you cannot push to, choosing the tracker warns: its files
would end up in your pull requests. Keep the issues in GitHub issues in a
repository of yours (--use github --repository owner/name), or set up
anyway (--anyway).

Options:
  -y, --yes                      Go ahead without asking for a yes
      --no-input                 Never ask, also at a terminal
      --use <tracker>            tracker: beads | github
      --repository <owner/name>  tracker: the GitHub repository, when the remote does not say
      --anyway                   tracker: set up a repository that looks like someone else's as your own
      --method <id>              program: the way to install, as `bend setup` lists them
      --keep <key>               facts: a saved fact to carry over (repeatable)
      --keep-all                 facts: carry all of them over
      --keep-none                facts: carry none over
      --rules <replace|keep>     instructions: what to do with rules changed by hand that are behind the current version
      --claude <link|rules>      instructions: what a CLAUDE.md of its own is to be: a link to AGENTS.md, or a file with the same rules

Options for every command:
  -C, --dir <path>     Run as if started in <path>
      --json           Print machine-readable JSON
      --text-file <f>  Read the text argument from a file ("-" for stdin)
      --as <name>      Who is acting, for the tracker's history
  -h, --help           Help for bend or for one command

$ bend version --help
[exit 0]
Which bend this is.

Usage:
  bend version

A number that goes up whenever bend's commands, options or JSON change,
for a program that runs bend to check it has one new enough.

Options for every command:
  -C, --dir <path>     Run as if started in <path>
      --json           Print machine-readable JSON
      --text-file <f>  Read the text argument from a file ("-" for stdin)
      --as <name>      Who is acting, for the tracker's history
  -h, --help           Help for bend or for one command

$ bend status
[exit 0]
Tracker   beads
Folder    <root>

Supported here
  ✓ sub-issues
  ✓ comments
  ✓ type
  ✓ priority
  ✓ assignee
  ✓ links: blocked-by, discovered-from, related
  ✓ description, done, plan, notes

Stored another way
  ~ category                         kept as the label category:<name>
  ~ requirements                     kept as a marked section inside the description
  ~ decisions and hand-overs         kept as comments with a fixed opening
  ~ ready for the owner to validate  a hand-over comment on an issue left in progress

Worth knowing
  ! The beads database is not synced anywhere: the issues exist on this machine only (see `bd dolt remote`).
Local copy
  Kept in      <root>/.git/bend/beads
  Last reread  never

$ bend -C <empty> setup
[exit 0]
Folder    <empty>

✗ tracker       Choose where the issues are kept
                Nothing says yet where this repository's issues are kept: in beads, a database inside the repository, or in GitHub issues.
                - Records the choice in `.bend.json` at the repository's top folder, a small file to check in, so it is the same for everyone who clones it.
                To do it: bend setup tracker
… program       Install beads
                Choose the tracker first.
… issues        Set up beads in this folder
                Choose the tracker first.
… instructions  Add Airbender's instructions for agents
                Choose the tracker first.
- facts         Carry saved facts over
                There is no issue database to hold saved facts.
… publish       Sync issues to the repository's remote
                Choose the tracker first.

✓ done   ✗ missing   … waits for an earlier step   - not needed here
To do every missing step in order: bend setup all
